notes: GitLab's source description creates a person-versus-persona modeling boundary for editorial review; it is not an adjudicated nationality finding.

value.object: private project containing cell financial and administrative records
value.assessment: almost certainly controlled by Kil-Nam Kang

sources.quote: We identified a private project almost certainly controlled by Kil-Nam Kang (강길남)

notes: GitLab's estimative-language assessment about historical project control. No project URL, credentials, present endpoint, or current-control claim is retained.

sources.quote: Kil-Nam Kang (강길남), a North Korean national managing a North Korean IT worker cell

notes: Publisher-reported management role; no legal finding or present organizational role is inferred.

sources.quote: Kang’s cell currently includes seven other North Korean nationals

notes: The source's 'currently' is bounded to its February 2026 publication. No present-day membership is asserted.

value.amount_qualifier: more than in summary; aggregated total in key findings

sources.quote: earnings of more than US$1.64 million between Q1 2022 and Q3 2025

sources.locator: Case Study 1, Key findings, aggregated financial data
sources.quote: We aggregated financial data and identified a total reported income of US$1.64 million from Q1 2022 to Q3 2025.

notes: Publisher-reported aggregate cell income, not a personal asset total, judgment, or independently audited figure. No account selectors are retained.

value.assessment: highly likely colocated and operating

sources.quote: We assess that the cell is highly likely colocated and operating from Beijing, China.

notes: Vendor assessment about the cell during the investigated period; not proof of Kang's current location or residence.

sources.locator: Case Study 1, Key findings, opening paragraph
sources.quote: Detailed financial records span from Q1 2022 to Q3 2025, however less detailed records indicate the cell was operating as early as 2019.

notes: Chronology derived from GitLab's reviewed project records, not a claim that Kang controlled every activity throughout the full period.

sources.locator: Case Study 1, Key findings, management paragraph
sources.quote: Records indicate that Kang managed the cell as two subteams in 2022, however from 2023 onwards only tracked performance at the individual level.

notes: Publisher-reported management chronology.

sources.locator: Case Study 1, Key findings, management paragraph
sources.quote: Kang maintains detailed personnel records, including dossiers on each team member, performance reviews

notes: Only high-level record categories are retained. Identity documents, credentials, device access, and personal dossier contents were excluded.

value.designation: Researcher at Kim Il-sung University Joint Research Center in Beijing
value.context: designation listed in cell personnel dossiers

sources.locator: Case Study 1, Key findings, personnel-dossier designation paragraph
sources.quote: Personnel dossiers list each of the cell members as “베이징주재 김일성종합대학 공동연구중심 연구사”, translating to “Researcher at Kim Il-sung University Joint Research Center in Beijing”.

sources.locator: Case Study 1, Key findings, personnel-dossier designation paragraph
sources.quote: This designation suggests that the cell’s presence in China may be under an academic pretext.

notes: A source-reported personnel-record designation and qualified interpretation, not independently verified university employment or affiliation.

value.activity: freelance and contract software development services

sources.quote: generates revenue through freelance software development under false identities

sources.locator: Case Study 1, Key findings, revenue-workflow paragraph
sources.quote: Financial records indicate that the cell generates revenue through freelance and contract software development services.

sources.locator: Case Study 1, Key findings, revenue-workflow paragraph
sources.quote: The cell focused on web and mobile app development.

notes: Cell-level publisher report, not verified lawful employment by Kang or every named member. Client, facilitator, payment, and identity selectors are excluded.

value.tracked_scope: quarterly individual income performance against targets
value.publisher_interpretation: regular monitoring and reporting to leadership

sources.locator: Case Study 1, Key findings, financial-monitoring paragraph
sources.quote: The project contained more than 120 spreadsheets, presentations, and documents that systematically track quarterly income performance for individual team members.

sources.locator: Case Study 1, Key findings, financial-monitoring paragraph
sources.quote: The comprehensiveness and highly structured nature of financial reports is indicative of regular financial monitoring and reporting to leadership.

notes: No underlying spreadsheets, client names, payment selectors, or personal performance data were collected.

value.publisher_finding: reviews confirmed physical colocation of the cell

sources.locator: Case Study 1, Key findings, performance-review paragraph
sources.quote: The private project also contained performance reviews for cell members, dated 2020. These performance reviews confirm that the cell is physically colocated

notes: Historical publisher finding about the cell. Review contents about household, ideology, and personal matters were not retained.

entities.identity_boundary: GitLab reports Kil-Nam Kang (강길남) as a North Korean natural person/operator who managed an IT-worker cell, while the current catalog models this record as a persona. Preserve that editorial model boundary: these are publisher assessments rather than an adjudication, and historical private-project evidence is historical; present control of any account or infrastructure requires current source evidence.

statements: Logpresso compared 1,879 publicly known DPRK-linked account patterns against 1,045,645 infostealer infection records collected from 2024 onward.

The method used email/account patterns, IP/subnet/ASN relationships, hardware IDs, and password-family similarity. Confidence was High for simultaneous IP+password+hardware overlap, Medium for two independent signals or one strong signal, and Low for one weak signal.
The filtered result contained 80 unique email accounts, 66 IP addresses, 66 hardware IDs, and access to 490 domains across 28 countries.
A single hardware device was associated with as many as five different employment personas/accounts, supporting centralized multi-identity operation.
Foreign-name personas sometimes exposed Korean OS/keyboard settings, and systematically varied password families connected otherwise separate accounts. No raw values are retained here.
Observed service categories formed a repeatable cycle: temporary SMS verification, VPN location masking, remote desktop, code/social/freelance platforms, and online payment services.
AS20485 TransTeleCom accounted for seven IPs tied to eleven accounts, Hong Kong represented 64.9% of events, and the report grouped the activity into five operational clusters.
